name: Peutz-Jeghers Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: World Health Organization (WHO) Criteria for Peutz-Jeghers Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of mucocutaneous melanin pigmentation on lips, buccal mucosa, fingers, or toes
Multiple hamartomatous polyps in the gastrointestinal tract confirmed by histology
Family history of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome in a first-degree relative

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of any two of the following: characteristic mucocutaneous pigmentation, multiple hamartomatous gastrointestinal polyps, or a family history of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for STK11 mutations can support diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.notes: Typically dark blue to brown macules around the mouth, lips, buccal mucosa, fingers, and toes
searchTerms: dark skin and mucous membrane spots
brown pigmentation on skin and mouth

pathognomonic.notes: Predominantly in small intestine but can occur throughout GI tract

common.notes: Due to polyp-related obstruction or intussusception
Common complication from polyps causing bowel obstruction

occasional.notes: May occur due to polyp burden or malabsorption
Due to chronic GI symptoms or malignancy
Occurs in male patients with PJS
searchTerms: testis tumors originating from Sertoli cells

rare.notes: Increased lifetime risk in PJS patients
Significantly elevated risk compared to general population

laboratory: Iron deficiency anemia due to chronic gastrointestinal bleeding
imaging: CT or MRI showing polyps and complications such as intussusception
genetic: Germline mutation in STK11 (LKB1) tumor suppressor gene
other: Histopathology confirming hamartomatous polyps with characteristic arborizing smooth muscle pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Juvenile polyps histologically distinct from hamartomatous polyps
Multiple hamartomas but with trichilemmomas and papillomatous papules

redFlags: Early onset malignancies (pancreatic, breast, or gastrointestinal cancers)
references: Giardiello FM, et al. Peutz-Jeghers syndrome: clinical and molecular features. Gut. 2000.
Hearle N, et al. Frequency and spectrum of cancers in the Peutz-Jeghers syndrome. Clin Cancer Res. 2006.
